title: Weather, nature & seasons
goal: Talk about the weather and the seasons, describe nature around you, and say what the weather is going to do.
intro: Odisha has a long hot summer, a heavy monsoon, a pleasant winter — and, on the coast, the threat of cyclones (**ବାତ୍ୟା**). Weather talk in Odia has no dummy 'it': instead, *rain happens* (ବର୍ଷା ହେଉଛି), *wind blows* (ପବନ ବହୁଛି), *cold falls* (ଥଣ୍ଡା ପଡ଼ୁଛି).

phrases.en: Shall we go to the beach?
The train is late because of fog.
A cyclone warning has been issued.

grammar.title: Weather expressions (no 'it')
grammar.body:
English needs a dummy subject ('*it* is raining'); Odia makes the weather itself the subject:

ବର୍ଷା **ହେଉଛି** — rain is happening — 'it's raining'
ଖରା **ହେଉଛି** / ଖରା **ଅଛି** — 'it's sunny'
ପବନ **ବହୁଛି** — wind is flowing — 'it's windy'
ଆକାଶରେ ମେଘ **ଘୋଡ଼ାଇଛି** — clouds have covered the sky
ଥଣ୍ଡା **ପଡ଼ୁଛି** — cold is falling — 'it's getting cold'

To say how *you* feel, use the dative (Unit 5): ମୋତେ ଶୀତ ଲାଗୁଛି 'I feel cold', ମୋତେ ଗରମ ଲାଗୁଛି 'I feel hot'.

grammar.title: 'It's going to …': future, ପରି ଲାଗୁଛି, -ବାକୁ ଯାଉଛି
grammar.body:
Three ways to talk about what's coming:

1. The plain **future** (Unit 17 has the full table; for 'it' the ending is **-ବ**): ବର୍ଷା ହେବ 'it will rain', ବାତ୍ୟା ଆସିବ 'a cyclone will come'.
2. **… ପରି ଲାଗୁଛି** 'it looks like …': ବର୍ଷା ହେବ ପରି ଲାଗୁଛି 'it looks like it'll rain'.
3. **-ବାକୁ ଯାଉଛି** 'is about to': ବର୍ଷା ହେବାକୁ ଯାଉଛି 'it's about to rain'.

examples.en: It looks like it's going to rain.
It's about to rain — take an umbrella.
The heat will rise next week.

dialogue.title: A day trip to Puri?
dialogue.setting: Sam and Lipi want to go to the beach at Puri, but the sky looks doubtful.

lines.speaker: Sam
lines.native: ଆଜି ପୁରୀ ଯିବା କି? ପାଗ କେମିତି ଅଛି?
lines.roman: aji Puri jiba ki? pagô kemiti ôchhi?
lines.en: Shall we go to Puri today? What's the weather like?

lines.speaker: Lipi
lines.native: ସକାଳୁ ଖରା ଥିଲା, କିନ୍ତୁ ଏବେ ମେଘ ଘୋଡ଼ାଇଛି।
lines.roman: sôkaḷu khôra thila, kintu ebe meghô ghoṛaichhi.
lines.en: It was sunny this morning, but now it's clouded over.

lines.speaker: Lipi
lines.native: ହେବ ପରି ଲାଗୁଛି। ଟିଭିରେ କହିଲେ, ସଞ୍ଜରେ ଘଡ଼ଘଡ଼ି ସହ ବର୍ଷା ହେବ।
lines.roman: hebô pôri laguchhi. ṭibhire kôhile, sôñjôre ghôṛôghôṛi sôhô bôrsa hebô.
lines.en: Looks like it. They said on TV there'll be thunderstorms in the evening.

lines.speaker: Sam
lines.en: It's not a cyclone, is it?

lines.speaker: Lipi
lines.native: ନା ନା। ବାତ୍ୟା ସାଧାରଣତଃ ଅକ୍ଟୋବର-ନଭେମ୍ବରରେ ଆସେ।
lines.roman: na na. battya sadharôṇôtô ôkṭobôrô-nôbhembôrôre ase.
lines.en: No, no. Cyclones usually come in October–November.

lines.speaker: Sam
lines.en: Then let's go in the morning and come back during the day.

lines.speaker: Lipi
lines.native: ଶୀତଦିନ। ପାଗ ଥଣ୍ଡା, ଆକାଶ ସଫା, ଆଉ ପିଠା ଖାଇବାର ସମୟ!
lines.roman: sitôdinô. pagô thôṇḍa, akasô sôpha, au piṭha khaibarô sômôyô!
lines.en: Winter. It's cool, the sky is clear, and it's time for eating piṭha (rice cakes)!

culture: Odisha's coast is hit by cyclones every few years — the 1999 Super Cyclone killed thousands, but today's early-warning and evacuation system is a model for the world, and Odias follow cyclone news (ବାତ୍ୟା ସତର୍କତା) closely. The monsoon arrives in June around the time of Raja and Rath Yatra. Winter (December–February) is festival and picnic season, with *piṭha* (rice cakes) and visits to Chilika Lake to see migratory birds.

tip.title: No 'it' for the weather
tip.body:
- The weather itself is the subject: ବର୍ଷା **ହେଉଛି** 'it's raining' (rain is happening), ଖରା ହେଉଛି 'it's sunny'.
- Wind 'flows': ପବନ **ବହୁଛି** 'it's windy'. Cold 'falls': ଥଣ୍ଡା **ପଡ଼ୁଛି**.
- How *you* feel takes ମୋତେ: ମୋତେ ଗରମ **ଲାଗୁଛି** 'I feel hot'.

sentences.en: It's raining now.
It's windy today.
It's very sunny outside.
It's getting cold — close the window.

sentences.native: ମୋତେ ଗରମ ଲାଗୁଛି, ପଙ୍ଖା ଚଲାଇ ଦିଅ।
sentences.roman: mote gôrômô laguchhi, pôṅkha chôlai diô.
sentences.en: I feel hot — switch the fan on.
It's always windy here.
No clouds today — it's sunny.
What's the weather like there?

tip.title: It will…, it looks like…
tip.body:
- Future for 'it': **-ବ** — ବର୍ଷା **ହେବ** 'it will rain', ବର୍ଷା ହେବ ନାହିଁ 'it won't rain'.
- **… ପରି ଲାଗୁଛି** 'it looks like …': ଝଡ଼ ଆସିବ ପରି ଲାଗୁଛି.
- **-ବାକୁ ଯାଉଛି** 'about to': ବର୍ଷା ହେବାକୁ ଯାଉଛି.

sentences.en: It will rain this evening.

sentences.native: ଆକାଶ କଳା ହୋଇଛି, ଝଡ଼ ଆସିବ ପରି ଲାଗୁଛି।
sentences.roman: akasô kôḷa hoichhi, jhôṛô asibô pôri laguchhi.
sentences.en: The sky has gone dark — looks like a storm's coming.
Will there be a storm tomorrow?

sentences.native: ବର୍ଷା ହେବାକୁ ଯାଉଛି, ଶୀଘ୍ର ଘରକୁ ଚାଲ।
sentences.roman: bôrsa hebaku jauchhi, sighrô ghôrôku chalô.
sentences.en: It's about to rain — let's hurry home.

sentences.native: ଆଜି ବର୍ଷା ହେବ ନାହିଁ, ଆକାଶ ସଫା ଅଛି।
sentences.roman: aji bôrsa hebô nahiṃ, akasô sôpha ôchhi.
sentences.en: It won't rain today — the sky is clear.
Take an umbrella — there'll be thunder this evening.
It's thundering — don't go out.
There's no electricity after the storm.
Summer is very hot here.
In the rainy season it rains every day.
Which is your favourite season?
Winter mornings feel very cold.

sentences.native: ମୋ ଜାମା ଓଦା, ଶୁଖିଲା ଜାମା ଦିଅ।
sentences.roman: mo jama oda, sukhila jama diô.
sentences.en: My shirt is wet — give me a dry one.
The kids got soaked in the rain.
You get mangoes in summer.
Winter's coming — the weather's getting cold.

tip.title: Let's …: the -ବା form
tip.body:
- With ଆମେ the future ends in **-ବା**: ଯିବା 'we'll go', ବସିବା 'we'll sit'.
- Said as a suggestion, it means **let's**: ଚାଲ, ସମୁଦ୍ର କୂଳକୁ ଯିବା! 'come on, let's go to the beach!'
- As a question it's 'shall we?': ପାହାଡ଼କୁ ଯିବା?

sentences.en: Come on, let's walk on the beach.
Shall we go to the hills on Sunday?
Shall we climb up the hill?
Let's walk in the forest for a bit.
Let's sit under the tree — the sun's strong.
Let's go and see the moon on the beach.
There are lots of trees on the riverbank.
This flower is really beautiful.
Lots of stars in the sky tonight.
No sun in the sky, only clouds.

tip.title: Because of …: ଯୋଗୁଁ
tip.body:
- **ଯୋଗୁଁ** comes *after* the cause: ବର୍ଷା **ଯୋଗୁଁ** 'because of the rain'.
- Then the result: ବର୍ଷା ଯୋଗୁଁ ବସ୍ ଡେରି 'the bus is late because of the rain'.
- You'll hear it on every weather warning: ବାତ୍ୟା ଯୋଗୁଁ …

sentences.en: The shops are shut because of the cyclone.
The bus is late because of the rain.
Drive slowly — it’s foggy.
The road is closed because of the flood.
My head aches because of the heat.
No electricity because of the cyclone.
There are floods here in the monsoon.
When will the cyclone hit?
It’s very foggy this morning.
Stay indoors during the storm.
